content: I slept and dreamt that life was joy. I awoke and saw that life was service. I acted and behold, service was joy.
author: Rabindranath Tagore
explanation:
Youth often imagines that happiness is found in passive pleasure and effortless ease. Maturity awakens to the demanding reality of duty, labor, and mutual responsibility. But the highest spiritual maturity discovers the ultimate paradox: that duty, when undertaken with love and wholehearted devotion, transforms into the purest and most enduring joy a human being can experience.

Joy and service are not enemies; they are the flower and the fruit of a life lived in harmony with the greater whole.
practicalInsight: Reframe a mundane chore or professional duty today not as a burdensome chore, but as a deliberate offering of service to the people you care about.
reflectionPrompt: How can you bring the spirit of craftsmanship and love into your daily responsibilities so that duty becomes a source of joy?
